title: Reserved pool failsafe: latency trigger window mismatch leads to underprovision and customer escalations
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Summary: Multiple customers reported sustained request throttling during short multi-minute traffic surges despite healthy aggregate capacity in reserved pools. Root cause appears to be a mismatch between autoscaler latency-based triggers (short 30s window) and reserved pool burst-accounting (5m ledger), which caused the controller to consider headroom sufficient while burst credits were being consumed. This manifested as repeated shortfalls for bursty tenants and several escalations from two S1 customers.

Scope: Affects Dedicated tenants using reserved pools with burst enabled across three regions (us-west-2, eu-west-1, us-east-1). Impact observed for tenants with high request fanout and low steady-state QPS but frequent tens-of-seconds spikes. Estimated 6 customers experienced elevated error rates; 2 reported user-facing throttles and opened support escalations.

Why this is unique: Previous incidents were primarily autoscaler signal delays or warmup bugs; this ticket investigates an interplay between trigger aggregation windows and burst-accounting reconciliation that causes the controller to underprovision during legitimate short surges even though long-run metrics look healthy.

Goals: 1) Provide immediate mitigation to stop customer throttles, 2) ship a technical fix to align trigger windows with burst accounting and add hysteresis, 3) add observability and alerts to detect the pattern proactively, 4) complete postmortem and customer comms.
repro_steps: 1) Create a dedicated reserved pool tenant with burst enabled and low steady QPS (e.g., 10 rps).
2) Generate synthetic traffic with repeated 20-90s spikes at 20x baseline every 3-6 minutes for 30 minutes.
3) Observe autoscaler: latency-based trigger averages over 30s do not fire additional reservation, while burst ledger drains across 5m windows and headroom estimate remains stale.
4) Verify request shaping / throttles appear and client error rate climbs despite cluster-level available GPU slots.
5) Confirm logs: controller decision shows 'headroom_ok=true' while burst-accounting ledger shows credit negative for tenant during spike.
6) Replicate in staging using the stress script at infra/tools/bench/tenant_burst_repro.py and the headroom tracer profile enabled.

proposed_fix: Hotpatch (fast) - autoscaler-controller: change latency trigger aggregation from 30s to a sliding 5m window OR short-circuit decisions when burst-ledger indicates negative credits; include unit tests and immediate rollback flag.

Medium-term - dual-window logic: keep short 30s window for micro-burst sensitivity AND longer 5m window for burst-accounting alignment; decision = scale if either window indicates sustained pressure or ledger negative with hysteresis counters.
Headroom estimator: introduce tenant-weighted predictive headroom using recent spike frequency to avoid oscillation and repeated small scale-ups/downs.
Safety limits: enforce max per-tenant scale-up rate and introduce a temporary overprovision budget for VIP customers to avoid customer-facing throttles during controller convergence.
Observability: add new Grafana panel for 'burst-ledger vs autoscaler-decision' and an alert when ledger negative + headroom_ok=true for >30s.
Customer mitigations: script to increase min_headroom for affected tenants and a playbook to toggle hotpatch rollback.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Canary: Deploy hotpatch to controller in us-west-2 to 5% of tenant traffic for 30m, monitor throttles and cost delta.
Phase 1 - Expanded Canary: If no regressions in 60m, increase to 25% across us-west-2 and eu-west-1 for 1 hour.
Phase 2 - Regional: 50% rollout to all affected regions for 2 hours with SRE on-call and rollback watch.
Phase 3 - Global: Full rollout and start medium-term dual-window change in a feature branch with staged canary after hotpatch stabilized.
Rollback criteria: increased client error rate >2x baseline for >5m, or sustained latency >p95 baseline + 200ms, or resource exhaustion on reserved pools.
Monitoring at each step: Grafana dashboard, controller traces, tenant-level burst ledger metric, per-tenant throttle rate and customer support channel.
